title: Make steward items above its limit approvable proposals
summary: The steward keeps the kind repeated-failure on an item above its limit. No request is queued for it, and approve-work and the status list only accept kind proposal. The fix is that anything above the limit is recorded as a proposal, so the owner can approve or reject it.

defaults_applied.how: Fix the kind assignment where the steward's items are validated, not the approve-work refusal for the two instances.
Add unit and CLI tests for the above-limit repeated-failure case; clippy and fmt stay clean.
Behavior criteria run cargo tests that exercise the approve path.
One focused change in the steward with its tests.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: The audience is the owner, who runs athena approve-work and athena status.

Root cause: validate_item in crates/athena-core/src/steward.rs maps the model's repeated-failure kind to WorkItemKind::RepeatedFailure regardless of rung, and find_open and open_proposals accept only Proposal. The fix is in the steward, so every item above the limit is a proposal. Widening approve-work to accept RepeatedFailure items is the rejected alternative.
The two existing records are under records/, which cannot change, so they are not converted here. The owner needs a new steward run, or a follow-up, to re-file them as proposals.
The repeated-failure kind stays for items within the limit, where a request is queued.

acceptance_criteria.text: A unit test in crates/athena-core/src/steward.rs passes a repeated-failure item on a rung above the role's limit through validation and decide. The resulting work item has kind Proposal and no request is queued. Run cargo test -p athena-core steward.

A repeated-failure item at or below the limit still becomes a RepeatedFailure work item with a queued request. The existing test scripted_output_with_a_real_gap_commits_the_work_items_and_a_queued_request still passes (cargo test -p athena-cli --test steward).

A CLI-level test runs the steward with a scripted repeated-failure item above the limit. The queued item appears in open_proposals (the list athena status shows) and approve_work accepts it instead of refusing. Run cargo test -p athena-cli.
The rule that anything above the steward's limit is a proposal, whatever kind the model named, is stated in a code comment or the design doc. If the steward prompt said otherwise, it is corrected.
cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy and cargo test pass for the workspace.

out_of_scope: Changing the steward's ladder or limits
Changing how approve-work builds its request
